mckinsey.name: Floors & Walkways
mckinsey.action: Following a comprehensive inspection of the damaged reception flooring, coordination was initiated with McKinsey to execute the recommended tile replacements. At the client's request, the reception tile replacement has been combined with the reception ceiling repair so that both works are executed together as a single project. The consolidated invoice covering both scopes has been shared with the McKinsey team, and the project is awaiting their feedback and formal approval to proceed to procurement and execution.
mckinsey.ref: Reception tile replacement and reception ceiling repair now bundled as one project at McKinsey's request, allowing both works to be carried out in a single exercise with minimal disruption to the reception area. Consolidated invoice submitted; feedback from the McKinsey team still awaited. Execution timeline to be confirmed upon approval.

mckinsey.name: Floors & Walkways cont.
mckinsey.action: Instability identified in the toilet hallway floor tiles, where a section previously caved in and was temporarily made safe. Vendor attended to assess the condition, following which the scope was expanded to cover the raised flooring across the wider office, which has been creaking. Second vendor review executed and scope confirmed. Invoice for the general office raised floor maintenance shared with the McKinsey team on 8 September 2026; feedback on execution is still awaited.
mckinsey.ref: Multiple creaks persist across the office floor. The toilet hallway remains under close observation as the critical point: the earlier cave-in was addressed with a temporary fix only, and the section could give way again at any time, presenting a trip and fall hazard in a high-traffic circulation area. Early approval is recommended so the permanent works can be executed across the office in a single exercise.

mckinsey.name: Ceiling (Zambezi Room)
mckinsey.action: Affected section of the Zambezi Room ceiling sits at the edge of the POP ceiling, making permanent remediation a delicate, higher-risk operation requiring a carefully sequenced approach to reinforce the structure and apply the final POP screeding finish without compromising the surrounding ceiling. Temporary VHF board was installed to mitigate the immediate structural risk pending permanent works. Following approval of the revised execution methodology and quote, the permanent reinforcement and POP screeding works were executed on 12 September 2026 and the temporary VHF boards removed.
mckinsey.ref: Zambezi Room ceiling permanent reinforcement and POP screeding completed on 12 September 2026, with the temporary support boards removed and the ceiling restored to a uniform finish. Structural risk resolved. Item closed.

mckinsey.name: Ceiling(Toilets)
mckinsey.action: Modification of the male and female restroom POP ceilings to incorporate accessible ceiling hatches, to facilitate maintenance access to the ceiling-mounted suction extractors within the restrooms. Following vendor assessment and agreement of scope, access panels were installed in both the male and female restrooms on 5 September 2026.
mckinsey.ref: Access panels installed on 5 September 2026 now provide permanent access for servicing and fault attendance on the ceiling-mounted extractors, removing the need to cut into the POP ceiling for future maintenance. Item closed.

mckinsey.name: Ceiling (Reception)
mckinsey.action: Repair required to the reception ceiling. At McKinsey's request, the works were combined with the reception tile replacement to be executed together as a single project, and the consolidated invoice covering both scopes was shared with the McKinsey team. On 23 September 2026, a ceiling board in the reception was reported displaced and dangling; a technician attended on 24 September 2026 and secured the board in place as a temporary measure.
mckinsey.ref: Following the 23 September incident, the matter has been escalated to the McKinsey team to expedite approval of the ceiling repair, recommending it proceed independently of the floor tile works if the tile replacement is not yet approved. The temporary fix holds the board in place, but the ceiling remains at risk of further displacement in a high-traffic, client-facing area until the permanent repair is carried out. Approval and execution timeline awaited.

The vendor further recommends that the cabinet be removed and resprayed off-site rather than in the office, to allow adequate curing time and avoid disruption to reception operations.
mckinsey.ref: Firm quote deferred by the vendor until an execution window is agreed. An estimated cost has been requested in the interim to support budgeting and scheduling decisions. Off-site respraying recommended, requiring temporary removal of the cabinet from reception; execution window to be agreed, ideally around a festive period when reduced occupancy minimises the impact of its absence.

mckinsey.name: UPS integrity test on the backup batteries.
mckinsey.action: UPS integrity test carried out on the 20kVA unit backup batteries. March 2026 test by Electrified Engineering Limited recorded 9 of 44 batteries in abnormal state, with approximately 20% of the bank fallen below the standard 12V threshold; two cells marked for replacement and the remainder rated fair condition. Battery health rated fair overall and replacement recommended. The follow-up test, scheduled for 27 June 2026, was deferred at the instruction of McKinsey management and executed by McKinsey's internal vendor on 31 July 2026, alongside the UPS preventive cycle and distribution board PPM.
mckinsey.ref: Vendor recommends replacement of the battery bank, as the reduced cell voltages shorten autonomous backup time. The integrity test report from McKinsey's internal vendor (31 July 2026) has not yet been shared with the facility team; findings are required to confirm current bank condition and progress the replacement decision. Report requested from McKinsey management. Priority item — UPS backup autonomy degraded pending replacement.

mckinsey.ref: Maintenance report shared by McKinsey and reviewed by the facility team — the only report received from the 31 July 2026 exercise. mckinsey.name: Electrical distribution board panels cont.
mckinsey.action: A series of power outages was recorded across multiple locations within the facility, each traced to a breaker tripping. On 15 June 2026 the kitchen socket tripped off. On 30 June 2026 the Nile Room experienced a power outage with equipment going offline; the electrical team was deployed and power restored. On 18 July 2026 a further outage affected the Nile Room and Reception, with the electrical team again responding to restore power and equipment. On 31 August 2026 breaker tripping recurred in the Nile Room and Reception area. In each case the affected equipment was brought back online following intervention.
mckinsey.ref: Four tripping incidents recorded over a ten-week period, with the Nile Room and Reception affected on three occasions, indicating a recurring fault rather than isolated events. Item yet to be treated. The latest distribution board maintenance report has been evaluated against previous years' reports to identify any deterioration or trend on the affected circuits. Monitoring ongoing for a further occurrence to pinpoint the exact breaker responsible, after which corrective action will be carried out.

mckinsey.name: MONTHLY ENERGY METER READING.
mckinsey.action: The facility energy consumption tracking matrix has been updated to incorporate the September 2026 data set. The definitive closing meter readings for the month were recorded at 64,926.4 kWh for the primary meter and 34,666.1 kWh for the secondary meter. The logging of these metrics ensures continuous visibility into facility power utilization trends through the third quarter of the operational year.
mckinsey.ref: Comparative analysis of the September closing metrics against the August readings shows the primary meter rising by +527.2 kWh (64,926.4 vs. 64,399.2 kWh), a 0.82% increase that reverses the reduction recorded in the previous cycle. The secondary meter continued its upward trajectory, increasing by +1,042.7 kWh (34,666.1 vs. 33,623.4 kWh), a 3.10% consumption expansion and an acceleration on the 2.15% rise recorded in August. Load growth therefore remains concentrated in the facility sub-zones tied to the secondary distribution infrastructure, while primary-side demand has resumed a modest upward movement.
